planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall into consistently moist, humus-rich soil, setting crowns at soil level and spacing plants about a foot apart in partial to full shade.

directions: Ellie is a compact simplicifolia-type astilbe producing dense, upright plumes of creamy white flowers over finely cut, glossy dark green foliage from midsummer into late summer. Its low, mounding habit keeps it well below arendsii-type astilbes, making it a good match for other dwarf simplicifolia selections such as 'Sprite' and 'Key West' along a shaded path or the front of a woodland border. Give it consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, since this fine-textured astilbe dries out and scorches quickly in sun or dry ground. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep the mound tight and floriferous.
